checks.command: NODE_BACKEND=js TMPDIR=/private/tmp ../aztec_experiments/.build/A02-node/node-v24.21.0-darwin-arm64/bin/node --test --test-name-pattern='sync has one owner|data HTTP waits|catch-up|new board read|concurrent reads coalesce|failed fresh sync|fresh read joins|close cancels one queued|status static and invalid' scripts/rolling-public-server.test.mjs

review: Read the two-file source/test diff before implementer conclusions. No other changed source paths and clean checkout at the candidate.

Admitted data reads reserve the shared queued cycle. A request arriving while an older acquisition is active cannot reuse that acquisition. One active and one queued cycle bound the mutation concurrency; pipelined reads coalesce.

The cycle resolves before its next setImmediate handoff, allowing waiting read continuations to query the validated snapshot without the next sync racing into the index busy state. No direct per-request index mutation owner is introduced.

Failed sync is explicit even when a controlled index still advertises an older ready snapshot. No-progress or missing revision ends read catch-up and returns not-ready. Catch-up continues only after a changed durable revision and yields between steps.

Close stops admission, clears timer/immediate, resolves queued readers closed, drains active sync and original handlers, then closes the index and optional relay. Existing disconnected-handler ownership machinery is preserved.

Required test changes match the new contract: a request waits for fresh validation after pre-existing sync, and a bounded cold catch-up may finish within that read. No assertion weakening or removed failure case found. Added cases cover policy advancement, concurrent admission, stale-on-error prevention, stalled catch-up, queued close, and non-data routes.

Structural review: one queue replaces the prior polling owner; no parallel lifecycle, per-request sync loop, new retry framework, or elapsed-time readiness assumption. setImmediate is scheduling fairness; deadline is failure bounding only.
tradeoffs: Every sequential data request now causes a fresh canonical validation, including sequential pagination. Concurrent admitted requests share a queued validation. Status, static and invalid routes do not add validation. This increases RPC work compared with a cached ready result and is the explicit freshness requirement, not a proven zero-RPC read path.
The production persistent index still owns canonical identity/deployment/anchor and per-step rechecks; this patch changes when its existing sync is invoked, not validation semantics.
limitations: Focused tests use labelled HTTP/index boundary doubles. No live chain operation, service restart, full browser journey or real-proof acceptance was performed by this review.
The read deadline is 20 seconds. This review does not qualify the separate unavailable-network latency target or the full RC40 acceptance envelope.
No deployment-load or sustained-concurrency benchmark was performed. Ready-state canonical RPC cost remains part of overall performance qualification.
